slides.page_title: Food Delivery App System Design: Cover

cover.title: Design a Scalable Food Delivery App
cover.subtitle: Zomato / Swiggy System Design
cover.tagline: Customers, restaurants and partners: 30M users, 3M orders/day, 300K restaurants, 400K partners. Order in under 3 s, deliver in about 30 min, never charge twice, never lose an order.

items: ==Three-sided marketplace==: customers order
Restaurants prepare the food
Delivery partners carry it to the door
Each side has its own app and **SLA**
Supply is ==geo-bound==: a restaurant serves about 5-7 km
So most systems **shard** by city or geo cell
Lunch 12-2pm and dinner 7-10pm: ~60% of daily orders
That is ~1.8M of 3M orders in 5 hours, ~100/s

blocks.note: radius 5-7 km, so shard by geo

blocks.title: Ask First in the Interview
items: Single city or national?
Own fleet or gig partners?
Scheduled orders?
Multi-restaurant carts?

blocks.title: Scope Rule
blocks.text: Three sides, hyperlocal supply, two daily peaks. Confirm scope and the 99% / 35 min / 3% targets before drawing boxes.
==Requirements== split into what each side can do (functional) and how well the system must do it (non-functional).

rows: search, menu, cart, pay, track, cancel, rate, reorder
accept/reject, mark ready, toggle item, edit menu
go online, get offers, accept, navigate, confirm pickup + drop

items: **99.95%** availability for ordering (about 22 min down/month)
p99 search latency **under 300 ms**
p99 checkout **under 2 s**
Orders: 35/s average, ==300/s== at peak (roughly 8x)
Browse is about 30x orders: ==10K QPS== search + menu reads
Notifications: 6 per order = 18M/day, peak near 1.5K/s
Pings are the ==largest write stream==, retained 7 days hot
Orders: 15 GB/day is about 5.5 TB/year
Menus and images add about 2 TB

blocks.title: Rule of thumb
blocks.text: QPS = daily volume x peak factor / 86,400 s. Do this first in every interview.

blocks.title: Design driver
blocks.text: Tracking writes (100K/s) dominate, not orders (300/s). Size storage and streams around pings.
The ==Food Delivery App== is split into an **edge**, ten core services, a Kafka event backbone and per-service data stores.

items: Edge: CDN for images and static menus
API gateway: auth, rate limiting, routing
Core: User, Catalog/Menu, Search, Cart, Order
Core: Payment, Dispatch, Tracking, Notification, Pricing/ETA
Sync (REST/gRPC) on the user-facing path
Async Kafka events after ==order placed==
Restaurant and dispatch both consume the event
Polyglot rule: each service owns its database
No cross-service joins; use events or APIs
Geo shard by city: Bengaluru outage spares Mumbai

blocks.title: Why split search?
blocks.text: Search takes ~30x more reads than orders, so it scales alone.

items: **Sync chain** of 6 services in checkout: latency adds up and failure odds multiply
Six services at 99.9% each give about 99.4% success
**One shared DB** for Order and Payment couples their deploys and outages
Checkout stays sync only up to order-placed
Everything after it is an async event
Each consumer scales on its own queue lag

blocks.title: Rule of thumb
blocks.text: Sync for what the user waits on, async for the rest.

cards.title: Edge
cards.text: CDN plus gateway guard the door.

cards.title: Data
cards.text: One owner per database, sharded by city.

blocks.title: 1. Responsibilities
items: List ==serviceable== restaurants near a location
Text search for dishes and cuisines
Filter and rank the candidates
**Serviceability first**: delivery polygon contains user, open now

blocks.title: 3. Index and Ranking
items: Geo index: ==geohash== or ==H3== cells; user cell plus neighbours, candidates in **under 50 ms**
ES index per city: `geo_point`, cuisine, rating, price band, nested `items`
Signals: relevance, distance, rating, ETA, promos, personalization
Score = weighted blend, then ML re-rank
Map lat/lng to H3 cell, add neighbour cells
Drop restaurants closed or outside polygon
Run text match on ES for dishes, cuisines
Blend scores, ML re-rank, return 20 per page
Autocomplete: trie or edge n-gram, p99 **under 100 ms**, typos edit distance 1-2

rows: id, geo, cuisines[], rating, is_open, avg_prep_min
Kafka CDC, search lag under 10 s

items: **Elasticsearch down**: serve cached top-50 per geo cell from Redis
**Stale index** shows a closed restaurant: cart and order steps re-verify availability
Hold items for one user and ==one restaurant==
Enforce the **single**-restaurant rule on every add
Price the cart and validate availability
Apply coupons, then hand a quote to Order
Cart in a Redis hash keyed `user_id`, ==24 h TTL==
Fast reads and writes; loss is tolerable
Server recomputes every price; **never** trust the client
Validate: restaurant open, items in stock
Validate: address serviceable, coupon valid
Compare with the cart price: unchanged?
If changed: show a diff, ==reconfirm== before payment

blocks.text: ==Quote token== = signed {price, expiry}; Order service **verifies** the amount without recomputing.

items: Rules: per-user limit, min order value, expiry
Redeem atomically in one Redis ==Lua script==
Script checks limit, then decrements, in one step
Redis loss empties carts: acceptable, **log** it
Rebuild from client state when possible
Coupon double redemption under concurrency
Fix: atomic decrement inside the Lua script

blocks.title: Rule of thumb
blocks.text: Client sends intent, server owns every rupee.

items: Own the ==order lifecycle== from cart handoff to delivery
Be the **single source of truth** for order status
Emit an event on every state transition
==Optimistic lock==: `UPDATE orders SET status=? WHERE id=? AND version=?` stops lost updates
Client sends `Idempotency-Key` on POST; **unique** constraint returns same order on retry
==Outbox==: order row + event row in one DB txn; relay publishes to Kafka, no dual-write loss
Acceptance timeout: **3 min** silence auto-rejects, refunds customer, may reroute
Cancel: free before ACCEPTED, partial fee after PREPARING, none after PICKED_UP
Order ==success rate== and restaurant acceptance rate
Time in each state, p50 and p90
Cancellation reasons, grouped by state
**Stuck-order count** (alert if PAYMENT_PENDING over 15 min)
Version column makes every transition a compare-and-set
Outbox row and order row commit together or not at all
Consumers dedupe on `event_id`, so replays are safe

blocks.title: Rule of thumb
blocks.text: Order service is the truth; every other service follows its events.

blocks.title: 1. Responsibilities
items: Collect money: ==UPI==, cards, wallets and COD
Refund, reconcile and stay **PCI-safe**
Never store raw card data
Gateway tokenization keeps PCI scope at the gateway
Create payment intent with an `idempotency_key`
Redirect to gateway, or send UPI collect
Gateway callback (==webhook==) reaches us
Mark **SUCCESS**; order moves to PLACED

blocks.title: 4. Data Model
items: `id`, `order_id`, `method`, `gateway`
`gateway_txn_id`, `status`, `idempotency_key`
`amount_paise` BIGINT: ₹249.50 = 24950
Integer paise only, never floats

blocks.title: 5. Key APIs
items: `POST /v1/payments` creates the intent
`POST /v1/webhooks/{gateway}` gateway callback
`POST /v1/payments/{id}/refund` full or partial

blocks.title: 6. Webhooks and Idempotency
items: Verify the ==HMAC== signature first
Dedupe by `gateway_txn_id` (unique)
Return **200** fast, process async
Idempotency key per attempt blocks double charge

blocks.title: 7. Pending and Routing
items: UPI timeout leaves status unknown
Poll status API at 10 s, 30 s, 2 min
Still unknown: reconcile job decides
Route by success rate per bank; Razorpay → Paytm

blocks.title: 8. Refunds and Failures
items: Cancel triggers partial or full refund
Ledger is append-only double entry
Debited but order not placed: recon finds it
Auto-refund within **24 hours**

blocks.title: 1. Responsibilities
items: Pick the {green:best partner} for each order
Minimize customer wait and delivery time
Balance earnings across partners
Supply: `GEOADD`/`GEOSEARCH` or H3 cells hold online, free partners
Trigger when prep time minus travel time ≈ 0, so the partner arrives as food is ready
Candidates: within 3 km, free or ending a drop, battery and vehicle checked
Score: pickup ETA, rating, acceptance history, batching fit, earnings fairness

blocks.title: 3. Offer Flow
items: 1. Take top candidate, push offer to ONE partner
2. Wait 15 s for accept
3. Decline or timeout: next candidate
4. Accept: assignment becomes ACCEPTED

blocks.title: 5. Key APIs
items: `POST /v1/dispatch/offers` (internal)
`POST /v1/partners/{id}/offers/{offer}/accept`
`PUT /v1/partners/{id}/status`

blocks.title: 7. Failure Scenarios
items: No partner at peak: widen radius, raise incentive, show longer ETA
Partner offline mid-order: auto-reassign with **priority boost**

blocks.title: 8. Key Metrics
items: Assignment time p90 under 60 s
Offer acceptance rate
Partner idle time
Orders per partner per hour
Claim before offering: one partner, one live offer
Two orders to one partner: CAS lets only one win
15 s timeout keeps the queue of candidates moving
Batch window of 5 s trades delay for global cost
Too early: partner idles at the restaurant
Too late: food goes cold on the counter
Start when prep minus travel is about ==0==

blocks.title: Rule of thumb
blocks.text: Claim the partner atomically before you offer the order.

slides.page_title: Live Tracking Pipeline and Data Model

blocks.title: 1. Responsibilities
items: {icon:android} **Ingest** partner GPS, ping every 4 s (10 s if stationary)
Show a ==live map== to the customer
Push ETA updates with each position
Peak load: about 100K writes/sec
Hot store: `partner:{id}:loc` in Redis, ==30 s TTL==
History to Cassandra with ==TTL 7 days==
Client channel: WebSocket or SSE per active order; fallback ==5 s long-poll==
Fan-out: subscribe by `order_id`; stream only active-order partners, not all 400K
App batches pings on poor networks; payload compressed to ~**60 bytes**
Gateway writes to Kafka, partitioned by `partner_id` so order is kept
Processor snaps GPS to roads (==map matching==), smooths with a Kalman filter
Last-write-wins by `ts`; a retried batch dedupes on (partner_id, ts)
Adaptive ping rate saves battery; push to subscribers of that order

blocks.title: 7. Key Metrics
items: Ping-to-screen latency ==p99 under 3 s==
Dropped-ping rate (alert on spikes)
Concurrent sockets: about **300K** at peak
Ingest: ~100K pings/sec x 60 B = ~6 MB/s

blocks.title: Rule of thumb
blocks.text: Show the last known position, never a blank map.

slides.subtitle: (Food Delivery App)

items: Only active-order partners are streamed, not all 400K
Redis holds the latest dot; Cassandra holds history
Reconnect with jitter so sockets do not stampede
Tell customers, restaurants and partners about ==state changes==
Four channels: push, SMS, in-app and email
Event-driven: consumes `order-events`, maps each to a template and audience
Channels: {icon:android} FCM and APNs push first
SMS fallback only for critical events (OTP, delivery PIN)
Event arrives on `order-events`; map to template and audience
Check preferences: opt-out, quiet hours, ==3 promo pushes/day==
Dedupe, then send on the best channel
Restaurant new-order ring repeats every ==30 s== until accepted
Fail: retry 1 s, 5 s, 30 s, then dead-letter queue after 3 failures
**Invalid or expired token**: prune on provider error codes
**Provider outage**: fail over push to SMS for ==critical only==
SMS for everything would blow up cost
Promo traffic never fails over; it just waits

blocks.title: Rule
blocks.text: Marketing must never block an order-accepted push.

items: ==ETA== = prep time + pickup travel + dropoff travel + handover buffer
__Prep time__: per-restaurant history by hour and order size
Kitchen-load signal (open orders) adds delay on busy nights
Travel: road graph routing with live traffic, p50 and p90 estimates
Users see a **range**, such as 28-35 min, not one number
Start with ==gradient boosted trees== as the first version
Features: restaurant, hour, order size, open orders, traffic
Retrain **daily** on completed orders
Serve in under 20 ms, inside the checkout path

lines: lo, hi = p50, p90   # shown range
blocks.note: prep time is the biggest term

items: Fee = ==distance slab== (0-2, 2-4, 4+ km) plus a demand multiplier
Surge: demand/supply ratio per geo cell over a **5-minute** window
Cap the multiplier at 2x and smooth it so it does not flap
Rain and peak hour: small extra fee and longer ETA, never reject orders
Late delivery costs more trust than a long ETA, so show p80

blocks.title: Summary
blocks.text: ETA = prep + pickup + drop + buffer; model it with trees, show p80, price by slab times a capped, smoothed surge.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Track ETA error per restaurant; prep time drifts first.

slides.page_title: ETA and Pricing Mistakes and Fixes

items: Straight-line distance: underestimates road distance by **30-40%**
Ignoring prep time, the largest source of ETA error
Rejecting orders in rain instead of adding a fee and ETA
Raw surge with no cap or smoothing, so prices flap

slides.subtitle: (Food Delivery App)

items: Scale ==reads first==: reads outnumber writes about **30:1**
CDN, Redis menu cache (TTL 60 s), search replicas
Shard orders, dispatch, tracking by city or geo cell
Hot cities get dedicated clusters
Pre-scale before 12 pm and 7 pm; autoscale on queue lag and QPS
Timeouts on every call; retries with ==jitter==
Circuit breakers stop calls to a sick dependency
Bulkheads: one pool per dependency
Multi-AZ active-active; DB failover RTO 60 s, RPO 0 for orders
One partner, two orders? Atomic claim: Redis `SET NX` lock plus offer state
Charge twice on retry? Idempotency key per attempt, dedupe `gateway_txn_id`
Restaurant never accepts? Auto-cancel after **3 min**, refund, reassign suggestion
10x scale or new country? More shards per city, regional stacks, local gateways
Retrying without jitter: a retry storm kills the dependency
One shared pool for all dependencies
Strong consistency for search: slow and pointless

blocks.title: Revision: Cheatsheet
blocks.text: 300 orders/s peak · 100K pings/s · 99.95% availability · 15 s offer timeout · 3 min acceptance timeout

items: Shed ==non-critical== first, protect checkout
Buy commodity, build differentiators
Strong money, eventual discovery

caption.text:
"How would you design Swiggy for millions of orders?" 🍔📱

This one question shows up in system design interviews all the time, and most people freeze. So I broke the whole thing down in handwritten notes, one subsystem at a time.

Here's what the carousel covers, in order:

📌 Problem statement and scope
📊 Requirements and scale estimates
🏗️ High-level architecture
🔍 Restaurant discovery and search
🛒 Cart and checkout
📦 Order service and the order state machine
💳 Payments
🛵 Delivery partner assignment
📍 Real-time order tracking
🔔 Notifications
⏱️ ETA prediction and dynamic pricing
⚖️ Scaling, failure handling, trade-offs and interview questions

Save this for your next interview prep session and share it with a friend who's preparing for SDE rounds.
